title: Reinforcing a Teams Identity
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note examines how long-tenured teams develop a shared identity -- scrappy, innovative, contrarian, and so on -- built from a history of how they've collectively overcome challenges. That identity, once named and reinforced, becomes a source of pride and confidence that shapes how the team approaches new work. The piece notes that identity can emerge organically or be strategically proposed by a leader who names a pattern they see and invites the team to adopt it, and argues that a leader's core job in either case is to notice and reinforce the identity once it exists.
points: Long-tenured teams develop shared identities (scrappy, innovative, contrarian) from their history of shared challenges.
A reinforced team identity builds confidence and pride, and shapes how members approach new work.
Team identity can emerge organically or be strategically proposed and named by a leader.
Leaders' core role is described as noticing an emerging identity and reinforcing it consistently.
A strong collective identity is linked to greater team resilience and collaborative spirit.
quotes: Teams that work together over a long period of time commonly develop an identity distinct from the organization’s culture.
A strong identity breeds confidence and allows the team to stand strong when challenged.
Good leaders listen for this emerging identity and reinforce it.
some leaders take a more strategic approach and promote an identity that doesn’t yet exist.
team identities shape experience and create expectations. How does your team see itself?
